full_judgment: 26. In regards handing over possession of the suit property to the defendant, learned Advocate for the petitioner has drawn this Court's attention to the oral and documentary evidence to substantiate that the actual possession of the property has not been handed over to the defendant. To prove her possession, the plaintiff herself stated in her deposition that she did not hand over physical possession of the suit property to the defendant and she herself was owning and possessing the suit property by residing herself therein and through tenants and the concerned utility bills and other taxes of the Government were paid by her. Other PWs supported this contention of the plaintiff. The defendant adduced four oral witnesses including himself to prove his possession in the suit property. Admittedly, the defendant was residing with his sister, the plaintiff from his childhood and the plaintiff looked after him but this fact of possession cannot be construed as possession of the defendant in the suit property on the basis of the disputed gift. Additionally, the plaintiff adduced some documentary evidence to prove her possession in the suit premises. It could not be proved by evidence of the defendant that after the execution of the deed of gift the plaintiff had left the disputed house and she was residing elsewhere. From the documentary evidence produced by the plaintiff it appears that though the gift was purported to be made in 1978, the holding of the suit property was in the name of the plaintiff [Exhibit-1(a)] after 1978, she paid holding tax [tax receipt number 16144 dated 18-3-1983, Exhibit-1(b)J. There was no separate holding in the name of the defendant and the suit premises existed as homestead even before the execution of the gift as evidenced by SA Khatian [Exhibit-2(b)). The electricity bills of the house stands in the name of the plaintiff (Exhibit-3) and municipality tax was collected from the plaintiff for the years 1983, 1984, 1981 and 1982 [Exhibit 4(a) and 4(b)]. The plaintiff also produced some rent receipts (Exhibit-5 series) showing that she was possessing the suit premises by leasing out the same to the tenants and PW 4 was adduced to prove the tenancy. The defendant produced a compromise agreement (Aposhnama) dated 18-2-1983 [Exhibit-(C)] entered into between the plaintiff and the defendant in which the defendnat admitted that the life interest of the subject matter of the gift would be retained by the plaintiff.
